newsitem.title: UK: Saudi tender news boosts UK barley futures.
newsitem.headline: Saudi tender news boosts UK barley futures.

text.p: News that Saudi Arabia is to tender for 1.72 million tonnes of feed barley on September 20 boosted UK feed barley futures on Wednesday.
Forward barley futures rose by as much as 1.10 stg a tonne, although turnover was low.
"People think most of the barley will come from the EU and as British barley is the cheapest the bulk will come from our market," said a trader.
Cash traders said it was almost impossible to buy barley off the farms.
"Farmers have seen the prices going up and they are hanging on for even higher prices," said a trader.

After starting the day lower, wheat futures appeared to get caught in spill-over sentiment from barley and closed with nearby months 0.70 to 0.95 stg up while forward positions were around 0.50 stg down after trading 337 lots.
Barley closed with Sep 0.25 stg up while Nov was 1.10 stg higher and Jan one stg above Tuesday's close. Turnover was 115 lots.

News that the EU had published a regulation to end the export tax on soft wheat came after the market closed. However, traders said the news was friendly...."but it all depends on how much they will let us export," said one.
"I don't think the market will soar on Thursday because when you look at wheat futures it seems as if some people had already got wind of this before the market shut," said another.
Amsterdam milling wheat futures closed two marks down after trading four lots, all in October.
UK cash trade was quiet with no fob business reported and only light trade seen on the delivered market.
Feed barley in East Anglia was fetching 106 stg a tonne for Oct/Dec, 0.50 stg up, with 108.50 and 109 stg paid for Jan/Mar.
